description: A copy doesn't take what's before the source's committed size. In version 2 that's four bytes of padding, which nothing reads or writes, and which a read from 0 gives as the source has them. Since 92a926e a copy from 0 writes a root header of its own, which has zeros there, so with garbage in the source's padding, a read from 0 on the replica differs from what was sent, and in exactly those four bytes: the same source with zeros there reads the same as the replica. An incremental sync leaves them as they are on both sides. replicate-version-1 is the same for version 1, whose copy of the root slot is there instead.

ops.note: with the garbage, as it's the source's own bytes
another copy, whose source is then given zeros in its padding
a copy reads back with zeros in its padding, as the replica does
the replica's padding doesn't come into it
